principle: A rule that names specific words is a rule that will miss the next word. Every rule here is stated as a measurement, so it applies to any corpus, any domain and any language the parser handles, including knowledge the model does not have yet. The recurring failure in this project was hand-written blocklists that kept missing the obvious case: 'monitoring' was listed and 'monitor' was not, 'approach' was listed and 'this approach' was not. Nothing below depends on a list of words.

entity_rules.name: an entity is a noun phrase
entity_rules.why: A verb, adjective, adverb or pronoun cannot be a thing a relation holds between. 'monitor causes proactive identification' passed the old rules because 'monitor' was not on a list; here it fails because 'monitor' is a VERB.

entity_rules.name: an entity is not a closed-class word
entity_rules.why: Pronouns and determiners refer to something else in the sentence. They are never knowledge on their own.

entity_rules.name: an entity is not the relation's own verb
entity_rules.why: The head noun of the relation cannot also be an endpoint of it. 'detection detects anomalies' says nothing.

entity_rules.name: an entity carries information about this corpus
entity_rules.why: This replaces every blocklist. A term that appears in most documents distinguishes nothing, whatever the term is. 'implementation' and 'approach' have low IDF in security prose because they are everywhere; 'MITRE' and 'YARA' have high IDF because they are not. The threshold does the work that a list of banned words was doing badly, and it does it for domains nobody has written a list for yet.

entity_rules.name: an entity is specific enough to name something
entity_rules.why: Single characters are noise; a clause is not an entity.

entity_rules.name: a word this corpus uses as a verb is not an entity
entity_rules.why: The parser tagged the bare subject monitor as PROPN, so a part-of-speech check alone let it through. What the corpus says about the word is a measurement, and it cannot miss a verb the way a list did.

relation_rules.name: both endpoints must be entities
relation_rules.why: If either end fails the entity rules the relation is not about anything.

relation_rules.name: the endpoints must differ
relation_rules.why: A relation from a thing to itself is a parse artefact.

relation_rules.name: the relation must be asserted more than once
relation_rules.why: One sentence can be a misparse. Three independent sentences are a claim the corpus makes.

relation_rules.name: frequency alone is not evidence
relation_rules.why: The highest-support relation on the real corpus was 'implementation requires careful consideration' at 16. A pair that appears in a large fraction of all documents is describing the writing style, not the subject. This is the same measurement as E4 applied to the pair rather than the term.

relation_rules.name: a specific relation outranks the general one it implies
relation_rules.why: If A--rel-->B and A--rel-->B-and-C both hold, keep the one that names more. The general one adds nothing and costs a node.

relation_rules.name: the relation must not be a paraphrase of its own endpoints
relation_rules.why: 'detection detects detection' and 'security requires security' carry no information. Measured by token overlap between the endpoints and the relation label.

application.where: every path that can add an edge to the graph
sources: a user prompt that states a fact
a model answer that is being promoted into the graph
application.note: A hand-written relation is checked too. The rules are not a filter for machine output; they are the definition of what counts as knowledge. If a rule rejects something a person wrote, either the rule is wrong or the fact is not a relation.
application.unknown_knowledge: Nothing here depends on the model already knowing the terms. E4 measures informativeness against the corpus in front of it, so a domain the model has never seen is handled by the same rule that handles security.

thresholds.note: Each is a measurement, not a word list. They are in one place so a corpus with different statistics can move them without editing code.
